Water, Fire, Keśava (Viṣṇu), Indra, Śacī, Sūrya, and the other lords [of the planets] correspond respectively to the decans (dreṣkāṇas).

When the Moon, Venus, Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, and others rise, the cloth is cold and so forth; it is thick and unwashed under the Moon, burnt by fire under Venus, middling under the Sun, firm under Mercury, and torn under Jupiter. (Śāravi)
The malefic and benefic planets should be situated in the Bahula and Sita divisions respectively.
(Vaiśvadevī) (Mandākrāntā) (Indravajrā)
And by the aspect of a wise planet situated in two houses, they produce twins within their own fortnight. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita, Upendravajrā,

They should bestow the fruits in the first, middle, and final stages of life.
(Indravajrā and Vasantatilakā meters)
For those who have resorted to false doctrines, there is enmity toward hearing [the truth], which is a refuge deep in the subtlety of inference; [this is] the *indravajrā* [meter]. (Śā.vi)
One incurs enmity with the leaders of guilds, kings, hunters, and those devoid of dharma; grief arises from affection; (Śārṅgadharapaddhati 105).

One receives honor produced by guilds, villages, cities, and officials; there is the acquisition of inferior grain; one suffers the rebuke of servants, children, and wife, and even attains physical deformity. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati 106).
Through dreams, thoughts, and one's own merits, it produces friendship with many men and the arrival of wealth for people; the attainment of results matures [from these]. (Mālinī meter)
One should declare that which is excessive as being subject to destruction;
having reached their respective periods, they shall yield their fruits.
(Vasantatilakā) From the Moon, a planet is auspicious when situated in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 11th, or 2nd houses;
from Venus, in the 6th, 12th, 11th, or 8th; and from Jupiter, in the 10th, 3rd, 11th, or 6th. (Śālinī)
(Prahārṣiṇī) (Prahārṣiṇī) (Prahārṣiṇī)

(In the Indravajrā and Puṣpitāgrā meters: He spoke words that were humble, skillful in meaning, and endowed with charm and renown.
If Venus (Śukra) is in the ascendant, he is skilled in the preparation of garments and similar crafts; if in the Sun, he is the son of a remarried woman.
If Jupiter (Jīva) is there, he becomes a city superintendent, a king, or a wealthy twice-born man.
The Śākyas, Ājīvikas, Bhikṣus, Vṛddhas, Carakas, Nirgranthas, and those who eat forest fare [are indicated by these planets].
In the *Pravrajyā* [Navāṃśa], there is a fall from one's own masters, who have been defeated by those stronger than oneself. (No specific name).
In *Kriyā*, one is lustful, has weak knees, unstable wealth, is brave, and is beloved by women;
marked on the palm of the hand with a spear, he is extremely fickle and very timid in water. (Śārṅgadharaviṣaya)
A man born when the Moon is in its own house (Cancer) is fond of water and gardens;

he is a hater of women, loves meat, frequents forests and mountains, becomes angry at improper acts for a long time, is courageous, firm-minded, haughty in spirit, and obedient to his mother. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita) A man born in the Sun's sign (Leo) is fond of water and gardens, lives in his own home, hates women, loves meat, frequents forests and mountains, becomes angry at improper acts for a long time, is courageous, firm-minded, haughty in spirit, and obedient to his mother. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita)
He is gentle, devoted to truth, skilled in the arts, knowledgeable in the meaning of the scriptures, and righteous.
Regarding daughters, he travels to foreign lands; he is pleasant of speech, has daughters as offspring, and few sons.
(Śārṅgadharapaddhati) He is eloquent, has large teeth, ears, lips, and nose, is industrious in action, and knows the crafts.
The one born under Aśvinī does not approach his enemies by force, but is won over by lineage and conciliation; he has beautiful eyes,
a thin waist, is firm in speech, endowed with good fortune, yet is indolent.

When Mars is situated in Kumbha (Aquarius), one is afflicted by suffering, destitute, wandering, devoted to falsehood, and harsh; when it is in Mṛga (Capricorn), one possesses abundant wealth and sons, or becomes a king, or at least equal to one.
(Āvi) (Upendravajrā) (Prahārṣiṇī)
In the *siṃha* [nakṣatra], there is a leader of forces; and that which was declared for the preceptor of the gods (*surejya*) in the lunar mansion of the moon (*candrabha*) [is also applicable].
In the sign of Aquarius, he has fruits like those of Cancer; in Capricorn, he is in his fall, possessing little wealth and lacking happiness.
(Śārdūlavikrīḍita, Puṣpitāgrā, and Aupacchandasika meters)
(Mandākrāntā) (Prahārṣiṇī) When Mars is in Aries,
when Saturn is in Libra, and when Rāhu is in Leo, there is destruction of the night.
When [Saturn] has reached its own sign,
a constellation, or its exaltation, the native will possess wealth, many sons, and his own family; he will be rich in assets.
When the Moon is situated in the ninth, second, fifth, fourth, seventh, or eleventh house, there is good fortune, offspring, friends, kinsmen,
wealth, shares, and stability in dharma.
When Mars is in its own division, one is endowed with a wife, strength, ornaments, and courage; he is possessed of splendor and great daring.
(Rathoddhatā and Prahārṣiṇī meters)
If Mercury occupies the third house and is conjoined with Saturn while situated in a quadrant and aspected by the Sun,
and if both the Sun and the Moon are in their sign of debilitation and aspected by Saturn from the seventh house, [the native becomes] an artisan.
(Mandākrāntā) (Puṣpitāgrā) (Indravajrā)
If Venus is in the sign of Aries, the king’s wife will behave like a man, be unchaste, and have illicit relations with others.
If Venus is in Virgo, she will be a servant, engage in base acts, and be devoted to her husband; yet she will be wicked toward her children according to its own divisions. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

If the Moon is cruel, devoid of strength, and set, yet aspected by its own lord, or if it is in the seventh house conjoined with the Moon, then [the woman] is abandoned by her husband with his permission. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita)
(Verse in Puṣpitāgrā meter) Endowed with the remaining [qualities] and possessed of vigor, if there is an emergence of a mass of vital energy (*ojas*),
she becomes renowned on earth as one not merely skilled in a single scripture, but even a female expounder of Brahman (*brahmavādinī*). (Verse in Śālinī meter)
And when the malefics, having exhausted their cold-rayed [cooling] influence, simultaneously occupy the trines and other such positions.
Struck by wood, one goes to death when observed by the son of the Sun (Saturn).
When Mars is at its setting, [death] arises from the crushing of a machine; and when Saturn and the Moon rise together, they cause [death by] the ancestors, animals, and those in hell.
